Only on Wi-FiStories are only downloaded ahead of time on Wi-Fi, never on mobile data

On this phone

CyPress keeps what is yours on your phone. Here is what that means, and the few times it talks to anyone else.

Stored on this phone

  • Your sites and folders
  • Saved stories and highlights
  • Your reading history and reading stats
  • Your settings and theme
  • Copies of stories (and their photos, only if you turn on offline photos), so you can read without a connection

What is ever sent, and to whom

  • The sites you follow. Stories and photos load straight from them. The web version goes through a relay, because browsers can’t read most sites directly.
  • Google’s icon and font services. Site icons and some theme fonts. They see the site’s name or your internet address, never your reading.
  • Feedly, Google News and Bing News. Only when you search for new sites in words, or use Near you. They see the words you typed.
  • A full-story helper. Only when a story is cut short, CyPress may ask the Jina reader or Morss.it for the rest. They see that story’s address. It never tries to get past a paywall.
  • GitHub. The Android app checks about once a day for a new version.
  • Your own sync relay. Only if you turn on Sync, and everything is locked with your sync code first.

Nothing else

No accounts. No tracking. No ads. No analytics.

    Topics you follow

    A smart folder gathers stories from every feed that mention any of its keywords.

    Relay setup

    CyPress has no account and no server of ours, so your reading stays under your control. A relay is a tiny free service that only you own. It lets your devices sync, and it fetches feeds and articles for sites that block feed readers, including TechCrunch. It takes about five minutes to set up, and you can skip it unless you want sync.

    1. Create a free account at cloudflare.com, open Workers & Pages, and choose Create, then Worker.
    2. Replace the sample code with the code below, then deploy.
    3. Paste your worker address (it ends in workers.dev) below, then press Test.

    Your relay is running older code. Copy the code below, paste it over the old code in Cloudflare (Edit code), and press Deploy. It fixes more sites that block feed readers.

    Anyone who has your address can use it, so keep it private.

    To sync between devices

    1. Use the code above (it now includes sync). If you set up your relay before, paste it again and deploy.
    2. In Cloudflare, open Storage & Databases, then KV, and create a namespace named cypress-sync.
    3. Open your worker, go to Settings, then Bindings, add a KV namespace binding with the variable name SYNC, pick cypress-sync, and deploy.
    4. In CyPress Settings, open Sync and press Start sync. On your other device, press I have a code and type the code shown.
